items.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: After a bunch of years of trying to sound like Scott Hamilton, I realized that that’s not the way you have your own career is to sound just like someone else.

ctx.x: When you are in a situation like today when you have four tenor saxes, do you go out of your way to either play off what someone else is doing — try to play different from what someone else is doing, or do you just let it rip?

Well both. You gather inspiration from listening to the other saxophone players or anyone else in the band for that matter. I’m lucky enough to get to work with Dave McKenna quite a bit and almost every note he plays gives me some sort of inspiration. But you try and get inspiration from the other saxophone players, but you also try to play differently. After a bunch of years of trying to sound like Scott Hamilton, I realized that that’s not the way you have your own career is to sound just like someone else.…
What was it about him that you tried to emulate?
